# Claude Desktop Theme Tuner: a guide for AI agents

The tuner themes the Claude desktop app, in two ways:

- The Theme Tuner mod of Claude Code (the home page of the app designs for
  it): a setup JSON, applied in a Claude Code session with no DevTools. It
  sets the surfaces, texts, five roles, git colors and code theme of each
  mode, the contrast and a color or gradient backdrop.
- The first tuner, at /legacy: 13 colors per mode, a live preview of Claude,
  and a DevTools snippet the user runs in Claude to apply it.

You never need to click through the page. With the mod, call its tool with
the JSON (below). With the first tuner, put a theme in a link, and open or
screenshot the link.

App: https://rinn7e.com/claude-desktop-theme-tuner/
First tuner: https://rinn7e.com/claude-desktop-theme-tuner/legacy
Source (MIT): https://github.com/rinn7e/claude-desktop-theme-tuner
Every knob of the mod: https://github.com/rinn7e/claude-desktop-theme-tuner/blob/main/doc/mod-knobs.md

## The mod setup JSON

What the home page writes, and what the mod takes: in its pane, as
`/tuner <JSON>`, or from an agent through its `set_theme` tool (full name
`mcp__theme-tuner__set_theme`), whose input is this JSON.

    {
      "light": {
        "preset": "solarized-light",
        "name": "Paper",
        "anchors": { "surface-0": "#ede7d4" },
        "roles": { "accent": "#c0009f" }
      },
      "dark": {
        "preset": "dracula",
        "roles": { "danger": "#ff5555" },
        "git": { "added": "#50fa7b" },
        "codeTheme": "dracula"
      },
      "contrast": "more",
      "backdrop": { "gradient": { "stops": ["#1e1e2e", "#45475a"], "angle": 135 } }
    }

- `light`, `dark`: each optional. A mode left out keeps Claude's own colors.
- `preset`, `name`, `colors`: as in the link of the first tuner (below);
  the 13 colors map to the knobs, and Claude derives the rest.
- `anchors`: `surface-0` (sidebar and page, the darkest surface),
  `surface-1` (the conversation), `surface-2` (panels), `surface-3` (menus),
  `text-primary`, `text-secondary`, `text-muted`. Each wins over what the
  preset gives.
- `roles`: `accent`, `danger`, `success`, `warning`, `pro`, a seed each:
  Claude keeps the hue and sets the lightness. Keep the meaning (danger a
  red, success a green, warning an amber).
- `git`: `added`, `removed`, `modified`, `merged`, `closed`, `conflicting`,
  `draft`.
- `codeTheme`: the id of one of Claude's code themes; by default the one of
  the preset's name, where Claude has one.
- `contrast`: `"more"` for stronger borders and focus rings.
- `backdrop`: `{ "color": "#rrggbb" }`, or `{ "gradient": { "stops": [2 to
  16 colors], "angle": 0 to 360, "shape": "linear" or "radial" } }`.

A link opens the home with a setup, for the user to look at or tune:

    https://rinn7e.com/claude-desktop-theme-tuner/#theme=<setup JSON, URI-encoded>

Claude refuses a whole look that breaks its rules, and the tool answers with
the reason: the surfaces run from `surface-0`, the darkest, each as light
as the one before it or lighter, in both modes (a `surface-1` set alone takes
`surface-2` along); in light mode `surface-3` equals `surface-2` (leave it
out); `text-muted` is no stronger than `text-secondary`; text needs enough
contrast on every surface.

## The first tuner (/legacy)

### The link

    https://rinn7e.com/claude-desktop-theme-tuner/legacy#theme=<JSON, URI-encoded>

Add `&view=preview` to show only the preview of Claude, for screenshots. It
fills the window up to 1280px wide, so a window at least 700px wide shows the
whole mock. Without it, the link opens the full tuner with the theme loaded,
ready for the user to copy the snippet.

The JSON:

    {
      "light": {
        "preset": "solarized-light",
        "name": "Neon Solarized",
        "colors": { "accent": "#c0009f", "accentHover": "#a3008a" }
      },
      "dark": { "preset": "dracula" },
      "reduceMotion": false,
      "thinArrows": false
    }

- `light`, `dark`: each optional. A mode left out stays as Claude ships it.
- `preset`: a preset id (below) to start from. Optional.
- `colors`: overrides the preset's colors, as `#rrggbb`. Without a `preset`,
  all 13 colors are required.
- `name`: shown in the tuner and in the snippet. Optional.
- `reduceMotion`: true also turns off Claude's looping animations.
- `thinArrows`: true draws thin chevrons in place of Claude's filled triangle
  arrows.

Build the link with encodeURIComponent, for example:

    node -e 'const theme = {light: {preset: "solarized-light", colors: {accent: "#c0009f"}}}; console.log("https://rinn7e.com/claude-desktop-theme-tuner/legacy#theme=" + encodeURIComponent(JSON.stringify(theme)) + "&view=preview")'

### The 13 colors

Surfaces:
- `frame`: sidebar, title bar, menus
- `canvas`: chat area, composer, panes
- `raised`: cards, inputs
- `pressed`: hovered and stronger fills

Text:
- `text`: messages, titles
- `textSecondary`: labels, list rows, Claude's thinking and tool rows
- `textMuted`: hints, timestamps

Accent and lines:
- `accent`: links, buttons, focus rings, progress bars
- `accentHover`: the hovered accent
- `onAccent`: text and icons on accent buttons
- `line`: borders, applied at 22% and 40% opacity

Lists and washes:
- `selected`: the selected sidebar row; hover uses it at 27%
- `wash`: the user's message bubbles and neutral tints, applied at 10%

### Rules for a good theme

Contrast is WCAG contrast ratio. The tuner's own presets all pass these:

- `text`, `textSecondary` and `textMuted` at least 4.5 on both `canvas` and
  `frame`.
- `accent` at least 4.5 on `canvas`: one color serves both links and buttons,
  so a bright neon must be darkened to work as link text. Use the bright shade
  for `accentHover` or `selected` instead, where it is not text.
- `onAccent` at least 4.5 on `accent`.
- `text` at least 4.5 on `selected`, and `selected` clearly visible against
  `frame` (about 1.15 or more).
- `textSecondary` dimmer than `text`, at least 1.5 apart, so Claude's thinking
  reads apart from its replies; `textMuted` no brighter than `textSecondary`.
- `raised` and `pressed` visibly different from `canvas` and `frame`.

The first tuner (the link without `&view=preview`) shows these checks for the
current theme.

## Presets

Every preset's 13 colors, as JSON, to start from or to check contrast
against without a browser:

    https://rinn7e.com/claude-desktop-theme-tuner/presets.json

    [{ "id": "solarized-light", "name": "Solarized Light", "mode": "light",
       "palette": { "frame": "#eee8d5", "canvas": "#fdf6e3", ... } }, ...]

The ids:

Light: claude-light, github-light, pierre-light, vs-code-light, one-light,
catppuccin-latte, solarized-light, vitesse-light, min-light, rose-pine-dawn,
slack-ochin, gruvbox-light, meadow-light

Dark: claude-dark, github-dark, github-dark-dimmed, pierre-dark, vs-code-dark,
one-dark, dracula, dracula-soft, catppuccin-mocha, nord, solarized-dark,
vitesse-dark, min-dark, monokai, tokyo-night, night-owl, rose-pine, ayu-dark,
slack-dark, gruvbox-dark, groovy-lambda-black

## Screenshots of the first tuner

With a browser tool, open the `&view=preview` link and wait for an element
with the `data-ready` attribute. From a shell, Playwright does it in one
command:

    npx playwright screenshot --wait-for-selector "[data-ready]" --full-page "<link>" theme-1.png

If it fails because Playwright's browser is not installed, either install it
once with `npx playwright install chromium` (a one-time download) or open the links
in your browser tool instead. In a browser tool, navigate to each link and
take a screenshot; never fill in the color fields one by one.

## Recipe: "design me a theme"

In a Claude Code session with the mod: write the setup JSON from the user's
request and call `set_theme`. Claude paints it at once, so the user sees it
and asks for changes; send the whole setup again each time.

Elsewhere, with the first tuner:

1. Pick a starting preset from the user's request (its colors are in
   presets.json), or write all 13 colors.
2. Design the variants the user asked for, keeping the rules above.
3. Build one `&view=preview` link per variant and screenshot each.
4. Show the user the screenshots, each with its link without `&view=preview`.
5. The user opens the one they like. The tuner loads it and explains how to
   apply it: with the Theme Tuner mod (below), or by copying the snippet and
   running it in Claude's DevTools (Help > Troubleshooting > Enable Developer
   Mode). Running the snippet is the user's step, since it runs code in their
   Claude app.

## Applying a theme with the Theme Tuner mod

In Claude Code on desktop, the Theme Tuner mod applies a theme with no
DevTools, and keeps it across restarts. The user installs it once:

    /plugin install theme-tuner --marketplace rinn7e/claude-desktop-theme-tuner

Then, in a Claude Code session:

- The user sends `/tuner <link>` with any link above (or `/tuner
  solarized-light dracula`, preset ids per mode), or `/tuner` to open its
  pane.
- An agent in that session calls the mod's tool, `set_theme`, with the setup
  JSON above (the link's JSON is a setup too).

The mod themes Claude Code sessions only; the snippet themes the whole app.
